summary: The candidate captures the paper's main mathematical arc and all principal named theorems, including surgery presentation, Kirby calculus, the ribbon-graph functor, purification, and the RT invariant. Most shared statements and page locators are accurate, and the selected ribbon-Hopf and RT normalization conventions agree with the Gold reference. It is not comprehensive enough to be flawless: several foundational definitions and the lemmas that establish the representation-category and Kirby-invariance mechanisms are absent or only implicit. It also contains duplicate, over-fragmented, or weakly typed entries and records no explicit external attribution.
strengths: Includes the main RT invariant theorem with the correct Kirby-color and signature-normalization construction.
Covers every Gold-designated background theorem: Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby calculus, Turaev's ribbon-graph functor, and Turaev purification.
Faithfully records the Turaev-style ribbon Hopf convention, including Δ(v)=R_{21}R(v⊗v), θ_V=ρ_V(v), and the quantum-trace factor ρ_V(uv).
Correctly captures modular category, modular Hopf algebra, negligible module, Kirby color, surgery sum, and purification at a useful high level.
Entry IDs are stable and descriptive, page locators are plausible and consistent with the supplied source, and displayed LaTeX is generally balanced.
issues: Omits the Gold framed-link definition and the basic Hopf-algebra definition.

Omits the separate coproduct-monoidal, antipode-duality, R-matrix-braiding, and universal-twist lemmas; their combined conclusion is stated, but the supporting mathematical mechanism is not extracted.
Omits the modular-data entry defining dim(i), twist eigenvalues v_i, D²=Σ_i dim(i)², and Δ=Σ_i v_i^{-1}dim(i)², even though D and Δ are subsequently used in the normalization formula.

Does not extract the handle-slide invariance lemma, blow-up invariance lemma, or Kirby-presentation-independence proposition as distinct results; these are central proof infrastructure for the RT theorem.
The purification definition is circular and incomplete: it says to quotient by negligible morphisms without defining negligible morphisms or their trace-pairing condition.
The quantum-trace definition allows arbitrary f∈End_K(V), while the categorical-trace comparison relevant to Rep_fd(A) requires an A-linear endomorphism.
The representation-category result appears twice as near-identical propositions, producing unnecessary redundancy.
Several axioms already contained in definitions are fragmented into propositions, while several page-17 and page-18 explanatory observations are mislabeled as definitions.
The vague entry named '模 Hopf 代数' duplicates the modular-Hopf discussion and misspells its identifier as 'modular-hop-algebra'.
No structured external-attribution metadata is supplied for results explicitly originating with Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby, Turaev, or Reshetikhin–Turaev.

entryLevelComparison.assessment: The main theorem, hypotheses, orientation-sensitive conclusion, and pair-invariant extension are accurately represented.
Accurate surgery-presentation theorem with the essential closed, connected, oriented hypothesis.
Correctly lists framed isotopy, handle slides, and addition or deletion of a ±1-framed unknot.
Faithfully gives the functorial invariant and the scalar-valued closed-graph specialization.
The conclusion is correct, but it is duplicated by paper:prop:ribbon-hopf-rep-category and does not separately expose all four structural lemmas.
The formula and convention are correct, but the stated domain of f is too broad for the categorical-trace identification.
The quotient construction is recognized, but negligible morphisms and their defining condition are not supplied.
The definitions of D and Δ are absent despite their use in the RT normalization.
Handle-slide invariance is asserted only inside the final theorem rather than extracted as the key intermediate lemma.
The separate lemma showing that normalization removes the ±1 Kirby move is absent.
Blackboard framing is later mentioned, but the foundational definition of an oriented framed link and its integer framing data is not extracted.
Quasitriangular and ribbon Hopf algebras are included, but their underlying Hopf-algebra definition is omitted.
